findings.problem: 'Caught by Holmes in the empty locked room' is wrong. Holmes and Watson had broken into the room, and Rucastle came to its door and found THEM there. It also states as fact that he 'ran for his mastiff'; that is Violet's cry. The snapshot also drops all the context the reader has had since [12:169] (Holmes's theory that he imprisoned his daughter), so a tap here says only that a dog mauled him.
findings.evidence: [12:186] 'a man appeared at the door of the room ... Sherlock Holmes sprang forward and confronted him.' [12:189] 'I have caught you, have I?' [12:190] '“He's gone for the dog!” cried Miss Hunter.'
findings.fix: BODY: Holmes believes Rucastle has been keeping his daughter Alice prisoner. Confronted by Holmes at the door of the empty room, Rucastle rushed downstairs — Violet Hunter cried that he had gone for the dog — but his starving mastiff seized him instead. Watson shot it, and Rucastle was carried inside alive but badly mauled.

findings.problem: 'His mastiff mauled him when he set it loose' states as fact something the text never confirms. Toller says only that 'someone' loosed the dog, and Violet's 'He's gone for the dog!' is her own surmise.
findings.evidence: [12:193] 'Someone has loosed the dog. It's not been fed for two days.'
findings.fix: Replace the last sentence with: His own half-starved mastiff, loosed that evening, mauled him.

findings.where: first card from [12:201] (subtitle, fixed across snapshots)
findings.problem: The subtitle 'Alice Rucastle's suitor, a seaman' shows at [12:201], but his being a seaman is first stated by Holmes at [12:206]. This is a small leak, but the subtitle is fixed, so it also sits on the first card.
findings.evidence: [12:201] only 'she met Mr. Fowler at a friend's house'; [12:206] 'as a good seaman should be'
findings.fix: SUBTITLE: Alice Rucastle’s suitor (keep 'a persistent seaman' in the [12:209] body, where it is already stated).

findings.problem: The first card names the mastiff Carlo and says Toller manages it and lets it loose at night. The dog is not introduced until [12:132]. This is not concealed information, but it pre-empts the Carlo scene and the warning that follows.
findings.evidence: [12:115] gives only Toller's looks and drinking; [12:132] 'old Toller, my groom, is the only man who can do anything with him ... Toller lets him loose every night'
findings.fix: First card BODY: The Rucastles’ manservant — a rough, uncouth man with grizzled hair and whiskers who smells of drink and has twice been drunk since Violet Hunter arrived. His wife is the household’s only other servant. Then add a snapshot from [12:132] with the current body (groom, the only one who can manage the mastiff Carlo, lets it loose at night).

findings.where: card from [1:4] (only snapshot) as seen throughout story 12
findings.problem: The card says Watson is Holmes's former lodger, now married and back in practice. In this story he is living at Baker Street with Holmes.
findings.evidence: [12:5] 'we sat after breakfast on either side of a cheery fire in the old room at Baker Street'; [12:82] 'just as I was thinking of turning in ... find him in the same position when I came down to breakfast'
findings.fix: Use the snapshot proposed in S11-03 (from [11:0]), or for story 12 alone add one from [12:0]: BODY: A doctor and Holmes’s closest friend, who tells these stories. In this case he is again sharing Holmes’s rooms at Baker Street and goes with him to Winchester.

findings.problem: 'She helped Holmes and Watson search the locked wing' undersells her part and is slightly off: Holmes kept her out of the room. What she did was lock Mrs. Toller in the cellar and hand over Toller's keys.
findings.evidence: [12:176] 'That is Mrs. Toller in the cellar ... Here are his keys'; [12:179] 'we had better go in without you'
findings.fix: BODY: She locked Mrs. Toller in the cellar and gave Holmes the keys to the locked wing, though the prisoner had already gone. Watson later reports that she became head of a private school at Walsall, with considerable success.
